title: The sign on the library door
text: ‘[[Borrow|Keep|Buy|Sell]] books here’ is written [[in|at|by|of]] blue on the library door. Next to the words, a picture shows a bag full [[of|with|from|in]] books. The bag helps [[explain|say|tell|speak]] the idea. Children can take books home, read them and bring them back. This may make a child want to go in and choose a book.

title: A small cake for one
text: The bakery poster [[shows|looks|sees|watches]] one little cake on a plate. There is only one fork beside it. This [[tells|says|speaks|talks]] people they can buy a cake for themselves. Someone who does not have a party to [[go|visit|enter|join]] to may still [[want|wish|hope|look]] a small treat with a cup of tea.

title: The bookshop stamp card
text: A sign at the bookshop [[says|tells|speaks|talks]], ‘Buy five books and get your sixth book free.’ Next to the words, there is a picture [[of|for|at|by]] a card with five stamps [[on|in|at|over]] it. The picture shows customers how to get the free book. It also gives people who read a [[lot|many|much|few]] a reason to shop there again.

title: The clock on the washing machine
text: A woman puts clothes in the machine before she leaves [[for|to|at|on]] work. On her phone, she chooses a time for it to finish. She comes home when the washing ends. The advert uses her day to show how the timer [[works|does|makes|acts]]. Someone with a [[busy|noisy|quick|loud]] schedule may [[find|think|see|feel]] that useful.

title: The room after the party
text: The floor is covered [[in|of|from|at]] paper and crumbs after a party. A cleaner arrives, and the next shot [[shows|tells|explains|says]] the family sitting in a tidy room. The cleaning service [[sells|buys|spends|pays]] the time after the guests leave. Hosts who enjoy parties but [[dislike|object|complain|disapprove]] the work afterwards may see a [[reason|cause|sense|point]] to book.

title: A map that works without a signal
text: [[In|At|On|By]] the middle of a walk, two hikers [[reach|arrive|get|come]] a fork in the path and see that their phones have [[lost|missed|forgotten|failed]] their signal. One opens a map she downloaded before leaving. The problem gives viewers a clear reason to [[try|attempt|experiment|practise]] the app’s offline feature. They can see why saving the map in advance could matter on a walk far [[from|of|off|away]] the nearest town.

title: The drink that changes its label
text: A juice brand puts different local place names on [[otherwise|however|instead|rather]] identical bottles. In the advert, friends search a shelf [[for|after|about|of]] the name of their town. The game gives shoppers a reason to look closely [[at|on|to|by]] a product they might usually pass. Seeing a familiar name can [[make|cause|turn|get]] an everyday purchase feel more personal, [[even|still|yet|just]] though the drink inside each bottle is the same.

title: The review with one complaint
text: A shoe shop places a customer review beside a product photo. The review praises the shoes [[for|of|with|by]] long walks but says they [[took|lasted|spent|passed]] a week to feel comfortable. Keeping that detail makes the review [[sound|hear|listen|tell]] more like an account of real use. A shopper might [[trust|rely|depend|count]] the praise more because the same customer has also [[given|made|done|caused]] them a reason to think carefully about the purchase.

title: The mountain printed on the packaging
text: A chocolate bar wrapper shows a mountain much larger than the small farm [[named|called|titled|said]] on the back. The image may [[suggest|infer|propose|recommend]] purity and open space, although it says [[little|few|small|scarce]] about where the cocoa was grown. This gap [[between|among|amid|within]] atmosphere and information is common in packaging. A careful buyer might enjoy the design [[while|whereas|meanwhile|unless]] reading the smaller details separately.

title: An advert that repeats the wrong answer
text: A language app video shows a learner choosing the wrong word three times. On the fourth attempt, she laughs and uses it correctly in a conversation. Repetition turns failure [[into|to|as|for]] part of the learning [[process|procedure|progress|proceeding]]. Viewers who [[fear|scare|frighten|threaten]] making mistakes may find this more persuasive than a [[claim|demand|request|plea]] that lessons are easy, because the difficulty [[remains|keeps|rests|lasts]] visible.
